title: CLI Design Spec
description: Input shape for scripts/cli_design_audit.mjs — a normalized description of a CLI/TUI's runtime-compatibility and visual-design behavior, structured as booleans so it can be scored deterministically instead of by reading prose.

tool.description: Optional name of the CLI/TUI being audited, for report labeling only — not scored.

respectsNoColorEnv.description: True if `NO_COLOR` (and `TERM=dumb`) suppress ANSI color/styling output entirely.

colorHasNonColorFallback.description: True if every meaning conveyed by color (success/warning/error/etc.) is ALSO conveyed by a symbol, label, or text — color is never the only signal.

alignsColumns.description: True if table/box column alignment uses Unicode display-width (not raw string length), so CJK characters and emoji do not break layout.

respectsTerminalWidth.description: True if output reflows or truncates sanely at narrow widths (e.g. 40/80/120 columns) instead of wrapping unpredictably or overflowing.

prefixesLinesForGrep.description: True if streamed/log-style output lines carry a stable prefix (level, component, timestamp) that survives piping into grep/CI logs.

quietByDefault.description: True if default output is concise (no verbose/debug noise) with an explicit `--verbose`/`-v` opt-in for more.

hasProgressForLongOps.description: True if operations that can take a perceptible amount of time show a spinner (unknown duration) or a bar+ETA (known denominator) — never silence.

errorsToStderr.description: True if error and warning output is written to stderr, not stdout, so it survives `cmd > out.txt` and doesn't corrupt piped stdout.

exitCodesMeaningful.description: True if the process exit code distinguishes success (0) from distinct failure classes, not just 0-vs-1 for everything.

honorsPipeNotATty.description: True if the tool detects a non-TTY stdout (pipe, redirect, CI log) and strips interactive/decorative output (cursor control, live-redraw, ANSI) instead of dumping raw escape codes.
